title: Best Invoicing Software for Freelancers
dek: The best invoicing software for a freelancer is the one that gets you paid with the least fuss — and for many that means free. This guide picks by how you work: free-first invoicing, hands-off automation, or one tool for your whole admin, with an honest note on who each is wrong for.

seo.metaDescription: The best invoicing software for freelancers — Wave, Zoho Invoice, FreshBooks, Bonsai and more — with the best free picks and who each tool suits.

richText: For a freelancer, invoicing is the least glamorous and most important admin you do — it is how you get paid. The good news is that the tools are mature and several excellent ones are free, so the goal is not to find the most powerful option but the one that gets a professional invoice out and money in with the least friction. This guide sorts the leading tools by how you actually work: free-first invoicing, hands-off automation, or one tool that runs your whole freelance back office. For each, you will also see who it is the wrong choice for.

body.text: What a freelancer actually needs from invoicing

items: Clean, branded invoices you can send in a couple of minutes.
Accept card or bank payment so clients can pay from the invoice itself.
Auto-send repeat invoices and chase late payers without you nagging.
See what is paid, outstanding, and overdue at a glance for tax and cash flow.
As a one-person business, a free or low-cost plan is usually all you need.

body.text: The best invoicing tools for freelancers

body.richText: The tools below are the ones that consistently fit freelancers. Descriptions are based on each vendor's current documented plans, not on hands-on testing. Free tiers and pricing change often, so treat any detail as "at the time of writing" and confirm it on the vendor's own pricing page before you commit.

body.text: Wave — best free invoicing with accounting

body.richText: Wave is the standout free option: it offers unlimited invoices and clients at no cost, and pairs invoicing with genuine bookkeeping, so you can track income and expenses in the same place. For a freelancer watching every euro, that combination is hard to beat. You pay only when you accept online payments (a per-transaction fee) or add payroll, so the core invoicing stays free.

richText: freelancers who want free invoicing and simple accounting together.

body.text: Zoho Invoice — best polished free invoicing

body.richText: Zoho Invoice is a genuinely free, polished invoicing tool — professional templates, online payments, time tracking, and reminders — and it is a strong choice if invoicing is all you need. Its free plan does carry limits (for example on the number of clients), so it suits freelancers with a focused client list rather than a fast-growing roster.

richText: a professional, free invoicing tool for a manageable client list.

body.text: FreshBooks — best when you want billing on autopilot

body.richText: FreshBooks is a paid tool built around ease and automation: recurring invoices, automatic late-payment reminders, expense tracking, and well-regarded support. If invoicing is eating your time and you would rather it ran itself, FreshBooks is often worth the monthly fee. There is no permanent free plan, only a trial, so it is a paid-from-the-start choice aimed at freelancers with steady income.

richText: established freelancers who want polish, automation, and support and will pay for it.
you are on a tight budget — a free tool covers the basics well.

body.text: Bonsai and QuickBooks — the whole back office

body.richText: Some freelancers want more than invoicing. Bonsai bundles invoicing with contracts, proposals, and a light CRM, so your whole client admin lives in one tool — ideal if you juggle several clients and hate switching apps. QuickBooks leans the other way, toward full accounting and tax, which suits freelancers who need proper books, not just invoices. Both are paid.

items.question: What is the best free invoicing software for freelancers?
items.answerRichText: Wave and Zoho Invoice are the standout free options. Wave offers unlimited invoices and clients plus basic accounting, while Zoho Invoice gives polished, professional invoicing for free with some limits, such as on client numbers. Both let you get paid professionally at no cost.

items.question: Do freelancers need paid invoicing software?
items.answerRichText: Not necessarily. A free tool like Wave or Zoho Invoice covers professional invoicing and online payments well. Paid tools like FreshBooks or Bonsai add automation, contracts, and support that pay off once invoicing takes real time or you want your whole admin in one place.

items.question: Can I get paid directly through an invoice?
items.answerRichText: Yes. Most invoicing tools let you add an online payment option so clients can pay by card or bank transfer straight from the invoice. This usually carries a per-transaction fee, but it gets you paid faster than manual bank transfers.

items.question: Is invoicing software the same as accounting software?
items.answerRichText: Not quite. Invoicing software focuses on billing clients and getting paid; accounting software adds full bookkeeping, expenses, and tax. Some tools blur the line — Wave includes basic accounting, and QuickBooks is accounting-first — so pick based on whether you need books or just invoices.
